value_stream.name: Customer Pickup, Loading Zone & Will-Call Counter Operations

fields.Owner: CX (VS-13) / Customer Pickup Program Manager / Store Ops
fields.Volume: ~140,000–220,000 pickup transactions/month across 200 stores, measured continuously

workflows.name: Pickup SLA, Wait-Time & Customer Experience Measurement

Automation Opportunity: - SLA auto-measure from timestamps; CX feedback prompt; friction-signal alerts; store/region dashboards
Controls: - CTL-745 (ensure controlled execution — Pickup Experience, Exceptions, Chargeback & Analytics (PA-171.3).)
- CTL-745: SLA defined & measured; CX captured; breaches root-caused; store/region tracked
Cross-references: - links to VS-13 (CX/W65), VS-10/VS-16 (order timestamps), VS-28 (analytics), VS-63 (store comms), W4962/W4965/W4966/W4970 (SLA inputs), W4981 (improvement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **SLA-breach risk**: Slow ready/wait/load → CX failure/abandonment; mitigated by SLA measurement and root-cause action
- **Feedback-blindness risk**: No CX capture → unmeasured friction; mitigated by post-pickup VOC
- **Variance risk**: Poor-performing stores unidentified; mitigated by store/region breakdown
System Touchpoints: - CX/VOC (VS-13 W65); order mgmt timestamps (VS-10/VS-16); analytics (VS-28); store-comms (VS-63)

steps.activity: Define & measure the pickup SLA: order-ready time (from W4965), wait time at counter/bay (W4962/W4966), load time (W4970), and the end-to-end pickup duration; measure against the target and by store/region
Capture customer experience: post-pickup feedback (CSAT/NPS links VS-13 W65), friction signals (queue, not-ready, damage), and the pickup-journey VOC; integrate with VS-13 CX analytics
Review & act: monthly SLA/CX review by store/region, root-cause breaches (staffing, capacity, process), and feed continuous improvement (W4981) and the store-comms/task system (VS-63)

fields.Participants: Store Ops (VS-07), CX (VS-13), Inventory (VS-05), Ecommerce (VS-10), Finance (VS-17)
fields.Trigger: Customer no-show; hold period expiry; cancellation
fields.Volume: ~5–10 no-show/expiry events per store per week × 200 stores

Automation Opportunity: - Hold-expiry auto-flag; reminder automation; auto-restock/refund workflow; no-show analytics
Controls: - CTL-97 (ensure will-call release integrity & loading safety.)
- CTL-745: hold period enforced; expiry processed; refund/charge per policy; restocking-fee documented
Cross-references: - links to VS-10 (BOPIS hold), VS-05/VS-32 (restock), VS-16 (W101 refund), VS-17 (finance), VS-13 (CX), W4965 (staging), W4966 (reminders), W4977 (SLA)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stale-hold risk**: Goods held indefinitely → lost sale/staging congestion; mitigated by hold-expiry policy
- **Refund-error risk**: Refund/charge mis-processed (restocking fee, deposit); mitigated by the policy and finance reconciliation
- **Customer-dissatisfaction risk**: Restocking fee/expiry perceived as unfair → complaint (VS-13); mitigated by clear policy and reminders
System Touchpoints: - Order mgmt (VS-10/VS-16); inventory/restock (VS-05); returns (VS-32); finance/refund (VS-17/VS-16 W101); CX (VS-13); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Track holds & expiries: monitor the hold period per policy (e.g., BOPIS 5-day links VS-10), remind approaching-expiry customers (W4966), and identify no-shows

Manage expiry/cancellation: on expiry or cancellation, restock the staged goods (links VS-05, VS-32), reverse/release the reservation, process the refund/charge per policy (restocking fee where applicable), and update order status
Analyze & reduce no-shows: root-cause no-shows (notification, friction, customer), feed CX (VS-13), adjust reminder policy (W4966), and manage restocking-fee policy/fairness

fields.Participants: Loaders, Store Ops (VS-07), CX (VS-13), Returns (VS-32), Claims (VS-90), Inventory (VS-05)
fields.Trigger: Damage at loading (W4970); shortage/wrong item discovered; customer report
fields.Volume: ~10–20 loading exceptions per store per week × 200 stores

workflows.name: Loading Damage, Shortage & Wrong-Load Exception Resolution

Automation Opportunity: - Exception capture (photo/order); resolution workflow; root-cause tagging; recurrence analytics
Controls: - CTL-745 (ensure controlled execution — Pickup Experience, Exceptions, Chargeback & Analytics (PA-171.3).)
- CTL-745: exception documented; resolved (replace/refund); inventory reconciled; root-caused & CAPA'd
Cross-references: - links to VS-32 (returns), VS-90 (claims), VS-05 (inventory), VS-13 (CX/recovery), VS-147 (safety CAPA), W4965 (staging), W4970 (loading), W4981 (improvement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Customer-loss risk**: Unresolved damage/shortage → complaint/churn (VS-13); mitigated by prompt resolution and recovery
- **Inventory-error risk**: Exception not reconciled → variance (VS-05); mitigated by inventory reconciliation
- **Recurrence risk**: Same exception recurs; mitigated by root-cause/CAPA
System Touchpoints: - Order mgmt (VS-10/VS-16); returns (VS-32); claims (VS-90); inventory (VS-05); CX (VS-13); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Capture & assess the exception: at the bay or on customer report, document damage/shortage/wrong-load (photo, order, items), assess cause (loading error, staging error W4965, goods defect), and decide resolution

Resolve: replace/refund the damaged/short/wrong item (links VS-32 returns, VS-90 damage claims), re-load the correct/complete order (W4970), issue service recovery per CX policy (VS-13), and reconcile inventory
Root-cause & prevent: log the exception, root-cause (process/training/equipment), feed continuous improvement (W4981) and CAPA (VS-147 if safety), and prevent recurrence

fields.Participants: LP (VS-23), Counter Staff (W4962), Fraud (VS-125), CX (VS-13), Finance (VS-17)
fields.Trigger: Suspicious pickup; identity/ownership mismatch; fraud alert
fields.Volume: ~100–300 pickup-fraud attempts/at-risk events per year across 200 stores

Automation Opportunity: - ID/order auto-verify; fraud-pattern detection; risk-flag hold; high-value release-auth gate
Controls: - CTL-97 (ensure will-call release integrity & loading safety.)
- CTL-745: ID/order verified; flagged orders reviewed; fraud monitored (VS-125); high-value LP-controlled
Cross-references: - links to VS-23 (LP), VS-125 (fraud), VS-91 (identity/privacy), VS-100 (legal), W4962 (counter/release), W4976 (high-value loading)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Wrong-party-release risk**: Order released to non-owner → loss (VS-23); mitigated by ID/order verification
- **BOPIS/pickup-fraud risk**: Fraudulent pickups/returns (VS-125); mitigated by fraud detection and holds
- **High-value-theft risk**: High-value goods pilfered at pickup (VS-23); mitigated by release controls
System Touchpoints: - LP/fraud monitoring (VS-23/VS-125); order mgmt (VS-10/VS-16); identity (VS-91); analytics (VS-28); Legal (VS-100)

steps.activity: Verify identity & ownership at release: ID/order verification (W4962) to prevent wrong-party release, flagged-orders review (paid status, chargeback risk, fraud-flag links VS-125), and high-value release controls (VS-23)

Detect pickup-channel fraud: patterns (duplicate-pickup, identity fraud, collusion, refund-then-pickup, BOPIS-fraud), monitor via the fraud program (VS-125), and flag risky pickups for hold/verification
Investigate & recover: investigate confirmed fraud, recover goods/loss, escalate to law-enforcement/Legal (VS-100) where material, and feed the fraud program (VS-125) and analytics

fields.Owner: Customer Pickup Program Manager / Store Ops / Analytics

workflows.name: Pickup Program Performance Analytics & Continuous Improvement

Automation Opportunity: - Performance dashboards; bottleneck/root-cause analytics; improvement-tracking; best-practice sharing
Controls: - CTL-745 (ensure controlled execution — Pickup Experience, Exceptions, Chargeback & Analytics (PA-171.3).)
- CTL-745: monthly performance review; improvements prioritized/tracked; outcomes measured vs KPIs
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (analytics), VS-133 (OpEx), VS-63 (store comms), VS-149 (self-checkout tech), VS-19.4/VS-124 (training), W4961 (operating model), W4963/W4964 (capacity/layout), W4977–W4980 (metrics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Insight-inaction risk**: Analytics not actioned → repeat issues; mitigated by the improvement pipeline and tracking
- **Variance risk**: Poor stores not lifted; mitigated by store/region targeting and best-practice sharing
- **Over-automation risk**: Tech (VS-149) deployed without the human/safety model; mitigated by balanced improvement

steps.activity: Analyze program performance: SLA/CX (W4977), throughput/capacity (W4963), exceptions/fraud (W4979/W4980), safety (W4982), cost/revenue (W4983), by store/region; identify top/bottom performers and root causes

Identify & prioritize improvements: staffing/capacity, layout/wayfinding (W4964), appointment model (W4963), training (VS-19.4/VS-124), technology (VS-149 self-checkout/scan), and safety (VS-147); build the improvement pipeline
steps.r: Program Manager / Store Ops / CX / HSE

steps.activity: Execute & sustain: pilot/roll improvements via store-comms (VS-63), track outcomes vs KPIs, feed the operating model (W4961) and OpEx program (VS-133), and report to leadership

fields.Participants: HSE (VS-24), Customer Safety (VS-147), Store Ops (VS-07), Occupational Health (VS-83), Legal/Claims (VS-100/VS-26), LP (VS-23)
fields.Trigger: Loading-zone incident/near-miss; customer/staff injury; property damage
fields.Volume: ~2–5 incidents/near-misses per store per year × 200 stores

workflows.name: Loading-Zone Safety Incident, CAPA & Customer-Injury Response

Automation Opportunity: - Incident-reporting app; CCTV auto-tag; CAPA tracking; insurance/claims workflow
Controls: - CTL-745 (ensure controlled execution — Pickup Experience, Exceptions, Chargeback & Analytics (PA-171.3).)
- CTL-745: scene secured; incident documented; root-caused & CAPA'd; DOLE-reportable handled; insurance notified
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE/DOLE), VS-147 (premises safety/CAPA), VS-83 (occupational health), VS-26 (insurance), VS-100 (legal/claims), VS-27 (CCTV), W4969–W4973 (safety controls)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Injury risk**: Customer/staff forklift/load injury (VS-147); mitigated by the safety model (W4969–W4973) and CAPA
- **Liability risk**: Customer-injury claim (VS-147/VS-100); mitigated by incident documentation and insurance
- **Recurrence risk**: Same incident repeats; mitigated by root-cause/CAPA
System Touchpoints: - HSE/incident reporting (VS-24); customer safety CAPA (VS-147); CCTV (VS-27); occupational health (VS-83); insurance/claims (VS-26); legal (VS-100)

steps.activity: Respond to the incident: secure the scene, provide first aid/medical (links VS-83), document (photo/witness/CCTV VS-27), and report per the incident protocol (links VS-24, VS-147 W330 emergency response)

Investigate & CAPA: root-cause (equipment W4973, layout W4964, spotter W4971, procedure), corrective/preventive actions, equipment/tag-out if needed, and feed the customer-safety CAPA (VS-147) and DOLE reportable (VS-24)

Manage claims & liability: customer-injury/property claim (links VS-147 premises liability, VS-26 insurance, VS-100 legal), insurance notification, settlement, and lessons-learned to prevent recurrence

fields.Trigger: Chargeable pickup/loading service; fee policy; billing cycle
fields.Volume: ~20,000–35,000 chargeable loading/pickup events per month × 200 stores

workflows.name: Pickup Loading Service Chargeback, Fees & Documentation

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-flag chargeable events; auto-bill via POS/order mgmt; fee-revenue dashboards; waiver workflow
Controls: - CTL-745 (ensure controlled execution — Pickup Experience, Exceptions, Chargeback & Analytics (PA-171.3).)
- CTL-745: chargeable events defined; captured at event; billed & reconciled; waivers documented
Cross-references: - links to VS-08 (POS), VS-16 (order/AR), VS-17 (revenue), VS-11 (B2B), VS-118 (revenue assurance), VS-13 (CX/waiver), W4970 (loading), W4977 (SLA)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Revenue-leakage risk**: Chargeable service not billed (VS-118); mitigated by capture-at-event and reconciliation
- **Fairness risk**: Fees perceived as unfair → complaint/churn (VS-13); mitigated by transparent policy and waivers
- **Inconsistency risk**: Stores apply fees differently; mitigated by the standard policy
System Touchpoints: - POS (VS-08); order mgmt (VS-16); finance/revenue (VS-17); B2B (VS-11); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Define the chargeback/fee model: which pickup/loading services are chargeable (e.g., assisted loading, after-hours, oversized, B2B project staging), the fee structure, free-vs-charge thresholds, and the B2B/contract treatment (links VS-11)
Capture & bill: capture chargeable events at the bay/counter, bill via POS (VS-08) or order mgmt (VS-16), document the service (what/when/fee), and reconcile to revenue (VS-17)
Govern fairness & analytics: review fee fairness/CX impact (links VS-13), waivers for loyalty/B2B (VS-13/VS-11), fee-revenue analytics, and policy refinement

fields.Participants: Privacy/DPO (VS-91), Store Ops (VS-07), CX (VS-13), IT (VS-27), Legal (VS-100)

workflows.name: Customer Pickup Channel Data Privacy, Consent & Records Management

Automation Opportunity: - Data-minimization at capture; consent management; DSAR workflow; retention auto-disposal
Controls: - CTL-745 (ensure controlled execution — Pickup Experience, Exceptions, Chargeback & Analytics (PA-171.3).)
- CTL-745: data minimized & consented; purpose-limited; retention enforced; DSAR handled; audited (VS-91)
Cross-references: - links to VS-91 (privacy/DSAR W271), VS-88 (records/retention), VS-29 (master/consent), VS-27 (IT security), VS-21 (audit), W4962 (ID capture), W4966 (contact data)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-collection risk**: Capturing more than needed (RA 10173); mitigated by data minimization
- **Retention risk**: Records kept beyond need; mitigated by retention schedule (VS-88)
- **Breach risk**: Pickup customer data exposed; mitigated by security (VS-27) and breach response (VS-91)
System Touchpoints: - Privacy/consent (VS-91/VS-29); ID/identity (VS-91); records/retention (VS-88); IT security (VS-27); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Govern pickup customer data per RA 10173: minimize data captured at pickup (ID verification, contact for notification, vehicle — links VS-91), consent for marketing/contact, purpose limitation (pickup fulfillment only), and retention limits
Manage the data lifecycle & DSAR: capture/store/secure pickup records, handle data-subject requests (access/correction/deletion links VS-91 W271), and dispose per the retention schedule (links VS-88)
Audit & assure: periodic privacy audit of the pickup channel (links VS-91), breach response readiness (VS-91), and training of counter/loading staff on data minimization
